rows.title: The Taste of Things review: a feast for the senses
rows.comment: a gentle love story and a paean to the pleasures of a carefully prepared meal.
rows.verdict_le10: a gentle love story and a paean to the pleasures of a carefully prepared meal.
rows.dek_lead: Against this sweaty, sweary backdrop of contemporary cooking on screen, Tran Anh Hung’s The Taste of Things emerges as an endearing anachronism: a gentle love story and a paean to the pleasures of a carefully prepared meal.

rows.title: 'The Taste of Things' Review: Ephemeral Passions
rows.comment: though it feels somewhat more restrained.
rows.verdict_le10: though it feels somewhat more restrained.
rows.dek_lead: As a good student of Robert Bresson, Hung has never let his work get overly focused on story. There are few current directors, except maybe Terence Malick or Apichatpong Weerasethakul, more attuned to the specifics of atmosphere and place.
